summary: Bologna has tightened car access and paid parking over the past eighteen months: on-street tariffs rose on 2 May 2025 after years of freezes (up to 3.90 euro an hour in the innermost ring), and from 1 January 2026 hybrid cars of non-residents lost ZTL access. The city's Città 30 speed-limit scheme was annulled by the regional administrative court in January 2026 and replaced by a street-by-street plan planned for April 2026. Supply is being reshaped by the tram works, with the first Red Line vehicle unveiled in September 2026 and passenger service targeted for spring or summer 2027, and by the enlarged Staveco car park, which reopened in October 2025 with about 300 spaces. The Comune publishes a 10-minute availability feed for three central garages and open datasets on car parks and EV charging bays; the private operator APCOA runs Piazza VIII Agosto and Riva Reno, while Bomob, a company reported to coordinate parking income for the Comune, financed the Staveco extension and had managed the Tanari interchange car park, which is now in a dispute with its owner.

items.text: On-street parking tariffs rose from 2 May 2025: one hour went from 1.20 to 1.80 euro in the semi-peripheral ring, 1.50 to 2.20 in the semi-central ring, 1.80 to 2.90 in the historic centre and 2.40 to 3.90 in the Cerchia dei Mille. Monthly permits rose to between 60 and 100 euro, and the Comune put the extra income at about 5.4 million euro a year.
items.source_title: Quanto costa parcheggiare a Bologna (con l'aumento) - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: From 1 January 2026 the virtual ZTL permit for hybrid cars can only be issued to Bologna residents or companies based in the city, and hybrid owners must pay for on-street parking. The Comune counted about 10,259 non-resident hybrids losing access and 19,530 resident hybrids that keep access but now pay; fully electric cars stay free of ZTL and parking charges.
items.source_title: Ztl, stretta sulle auto ibride - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: The Bologna Welcome page, read on 21 October 2026 and undated, says the historic-centre ZTL is monitored by the Sirio electronic gates from 7:00 to 20:00 every day, with the pedestrian zones and the 'area T' (via Rizzoli, via Indipendenza, via Ugo Bassi) restricted around the clock. It also says a daily access ticket can be bought and links to the Comune's ZTL page.

The regional administrative court (TAR Emilia-Romagna) annulled the orders that lowered the speed limit to 30 km/h on almost all city roads, ruling the blanket measure disproportionate. The decision was not final, and the 30 km/h limit introduced in the historic centre from 31 December 2023 was not affected.
items.source_title: Il TAR ha annullato il provvedimento che istituiva la 'città 30' a Bologna - Il Post

items.text: The Comune approved a new Città 30 plan with a technical sheet justifying each street, covering 258 km of roads grouped in 47 zones, planned to take effect on 20 April 2026 with implementing orders to follow. The mayor had dropped an appeal to the Council of State to focus on this plan.
items.source_title: Il nuovo piano di Bologna per riattivare 'città 30' - Il Post

items.text: The Metropolitan City council approved the metropolitan sustainable urban mobility plan (PUMS) by resolution no. 54 of 27 November 2019. In the council debate the plan was described as foreseeing about 2.06 billion euro of investment to 2030, with the tram part of the core public-transport network.
items.source_title: Delibera del Consiglio metropolitano n. 54 del 27/11/2019 (approvazione PUMS) - pumsbologna.it

items.text: Council figures reported in October 2025 show parking spaces in the centre falling from 10,098 in 2013 to 9,227 in 2022 and 9,136 in December 2024. Standard blue-line spaces fell from 6,172 to 5,866 in two years, while resident white-line spaces rose from 1,110 to 1,271.
items.source_title: Parcheggi a Bologna, calo drastico. In 10 anni 1.000 in meno - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: The ex-Staveco car park on viale Panzacchi reopened on 20 October 2025 after works costing 2.8 million euro, going from under 180 to about 300 spaces with a raised modular steel deck and doubled, set-back entrances. Tariffs stayed unchanged at 2 euro per hour by day, 1 euro at night, 12 euro per day and 180 euro per month, with an electronic toll (telepedaggio) planned by November.
items.source_title: Cosa cambia al parcheggio Staveco di Bologna? - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: The Staveco extension was announced as financed by Bomob, described as the company that coordinates parking income and pays 70% of its earnings to the Comune. The 2.8 million euro cost was to be deducted from the fee Bomob pays the Comune.
items.source_title: Parcheggio Staveco, via ai lavori per i nuovi posti auto: diventeranno 305 - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: The Tanari car park beside the station belongs to FS Sistemi Urbani, which was asking the Comune to hand it back after the second extension of the loan for use expired. The report says it was open but unstaffed and degraded, a mediation meeting was planned for the end of January 2026, and Bomob had managed the structure.
items.source_title: Tanari, il parcheggio conteso - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: APCOA's page for Piazza VIII Agosto, undated and read on 21 October 2026, lists 702 spaces, 2 EV charging spaces, 24-hour opening and Telepass. It shows 3.30 euro per hour for hours 1 to 3, falling to 1.20 euro from the 11th hour, with a maximum daily rate of 25 euro.

The Bologna Welcome listing for the Riva Reno multi-storey car park, undated and read on 21 October 2026, gives 546 spaces, 24-hour attended operation, a 2.00 m height limit and an apcoa.it contact address. This indicates APCOA is the operator.
items.source_title: Parcheggio Via Riva Reno - Bologna Welcome

items.text: The Comune's open-data portal publishes 'Disponibilità Parcheggi (VIGENTE)', described as availability of public car parks with a reading every 10 minutes and only the latest reading kept, plus a separate historic dataset. It is licensed CC BY 4.0, the current table holds three garages (Autostazione, Riva Reno, VIII Agosto), and it was read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: Disponibilità Parcheggi (VIGENTE) - Open Data Comune di Bologna

items.text: The Comune's 'Parcheggi - strutture' open dataset, last modified 27 June 2024, lists 44 car park facilities with capacity and tariff type. Examples include Michelino (5,500), Nuovo Parcheggio Stazione (900), Fiera Parco Nord (750), Piazza otto agosto (700), Metropark (683), Riva Reno (543), Autostazione (280) and Staveco (180, before the extension).
items.source_title: Parcheggi - strutture - Open Data Comune di Bologna

items.text: The Comune's open dataset of EV charging parking, last modified 28 July 2025, lists 129 locations with 235 charging bays, of which 128 are active and 1 under construction. Operators are Be Charge (57 locations), Enel X (31), Hera (20), Enel (19) and Enermia (2), and 123 are 'quick' and 6 'fast'.
items.source_title: Parcheggi dotati di colonnine elettriche ricarica autoveicoli - Open Data Comune di Bologna

items.text: The Bologna Welcome parking guide, updated 24 March 2026, says parking is paid on blue lines and in public and private car parks, and free only in some interchange car parks. It lists Prati di Caprara, Antistadio (free if combined with a bike), Ferriera (free with a bus ticket), Santa Viola, Zaccherini Alvisi, Largo Lercaro and Piazza della Pace as interchange car parks.
items.source_title: Guida ai parcheggi di Bologna - Bologna Welcome

items.text: The tram Green Line plan was reported with a 6.9 km route and 17 stops from via dei Mille to Corticella. It planned a 200-space multi-storey car park between via Ferrarese and via del Saliceto and 197 surface spaces in via Bassanelli, with works to run to June 2026 under the PNRR recovery funds.
items.source_title: Tram Bologna, la Linea verde corre contro il tempo - Il Resto del Carlino

items.text: The first tram for the Red Line was unveiled at the Borgo Panigale depot on 9 September 2026, with a fleet of 35 trams ordered. The mayor said the aim is to be ready in spring 2027, subject to national approval, with first service between Borgo Panigale and the city centre and free rides in the first months.
items.source_title: Svelato il tram di Bologna giallo e oro in stile Iron Man - Il Resto del Carlino

gaps: No official Comune di Bologna ZTL, Rita permit or parking-tariff page could be read: https://www.comune.bologna.it/servizi-informazioni/zona-traffico-limitato-ztl and https://www.comune.bologna.it/servizi-informazioni/sosta-tariffe-abbonamenti returned only licence text, so ZTL and tariff facts rest on press and Bologna Welcome.
https://www.tper.it/parcheggi returned 403, so Tper's own parking offer, Sosta Bologna branding and any Tper role in parking could not be confirmed.

The operator of the Autostazione garage and any Saba or Indigo presence in Bologna could not be established from pages read; the only operator sources opened name APCOA (VIII Agosto, Riva Reno) and Bomob (Tanari, Staveco finance).
The role and legal form of Bomob and the on-street parking concession terms were only found in press mentions; no official concession document was opened.

Web search budget ran out before checking 2026 press on resident permits (Rita), the Guidazzi car park and any outcome of the Tanari mediation; the Green Line's cost increase and PNRR deadline (Il Resto del Carlino, 3 June 2026) were read but not included.

The Red Line passenger start date was not confirmed beyond the September 2026 statement of spring/summer 2027; the actual entry into force of the new Città 30 orders on 20 April 2026 was not verified.

No parking occupancy or usage statement from Tper or the Comune (beyond the open-data feed's existence) was found; browser-pane tab creation failed, so pages were read as raw text through a script, not in the browser pane.
